title: Frame an Analytical Decision
why: A decision question gives an analysis a purpose beyond finding interesting patterns.
activity: Choose an openly available or synthetic dataset and a decision question. Define audience, scope, success criteria, and what data cannot answer.
evidence: An analysis brief with a decision question and limits.
reflection: What decision could change because of your analysis?

title: Define Meaningful Measures
why: A metric is only useful when its definition and coverage are understood.
activity: Write a metric dictionary covering units, population, time window, and exclusions. Identify missing coverage, sampling bias, and inappropriate comparisons.
evidence: A metric dictionary and measurement risk notes.
reflection: Which population or time window is missing from your measure?

title: Retrieve and Validate Data
why: Incorrect joins and aggregations can produce plausible but misleading results.
activity: Write queries or equivalent structured retrieval steps. Validate row counts, keys, joins, and aggregations against small manually checked examples.
evidence: Retrieval queries, source/license notes, and validation examples.
reflection: How did you verify that retrieval did not multiply or omit rows?

title: Build a Cleaning Pipeline
why: Cleaning decisions affect which conclusions a dataset can support.
activity: Profile missingness, duplicates, and invalid values. Implement explicit transformation rules and keep a record of changed or excluded rows.
evidence: A repeatable cleaning pipeline and before/after quality report.
reflection: Which transformation most changed your sample or results?

title: Explore Patterns and Uncertainty
why: Exploration can reveal patterns without establishing their causes.
activity: Compare distributions and meaningful segments. Quantify uncertainty where appropriate and discuss confounders; do not turn correlation into a causal claim.
evidence: An analysis notebook with checks, figures, and uncertainty notes.
reflection: Which alternative explanation could account for the pattern you found?

title: Visualize the Decision
why: Chart choices affect how people interpret magnitude and uncertainty.
activity: Choose three charts tied to the original question. Label units, time windows, and sources; check scales, contrast, and color-independent interpretation.
evidence: Three accessible charts and design rationales.
reflection: Could someone interpret the main finding without relying on color?

title: Write an Evidence-Based Recommendation
why: A recommendation should follow from the evidence and acknowledge uncertainty.
activity: Write a short memo with a finding, supporting evidence, limitations, and a recommended action or next question. Separate facts from assumptions.
evidence: A decision memo linking claims to analysis outputs.
reflection: What additional evidence would change your recommendation?

title: Make the Analysis Reproducible
why: Reproducibility lets others check results and extend the work.
activity: Version inputs or record how to obtain them lawfully, document dependencies, and run the analysis from a clean setup. Add quality checks.
evidence: A rerunnable project, setup guide, and data quality checks.
reflection: Which dependency or data assumption initially blocked a clean rerun?

title: Review With a Stakeholder
why: Review can uncover analytical and communication mistakes before decisions depend on them.
activity: Ask a peer to challenge the memo and reproduce a result. Record feedback and fix one analytical or communication issue. State if the reviewer is a peer rather than a real stakeholder.
evidence: Review notes, reproduced results, and a revised memo.
reflection: Which challenge from the reviewer changed your conclusion?

title: Publish an Analytics Case Study
why: An analytics portfolio should connect a decision to reproducible evidence.
activity: Explain the decision, provenance, cleaning, analysis, visualization, recommendation, and uncertainty. Publish only permitted data or synthetic examples.
evidence: A reproducible case study with source/license details and limitations.
reflection: Which claims are supported by your data, and which are outside its scope?
